title: Prove multi-sandbox fan-out end to end against the live factory
description:
The evidence run that Phase 2's definition of done requires, and that ihf cannot close without.

Every cloud run so far has been one tick or zero working containers. Dispatch a real epic with at least 3 ready ticks in wave 1 and at least one dependent tick behind them, so BOTH the fan-out and the second-wave path (wiy) are exercised in one run.

Record, in a note on this tick: run id, per-tick container outcome, wall-clock per container, whether wave 2 fanned out to containers or fell back to the single-sandbox closeout path, and the run's cost from gateway telemetry.

Budget: this is a paid run. Keep the ticks small (toy-scale is fine — the subject under test is the substrate, not the code the workers write).
notes:
2026-08-22 13:51 - LIVE RUN run_2e66e765f74c4192b2b9a24a6e8415cf started 11:47:26Z — epic 72y, wave 1 = 201, 5jo, 5qj, gm5 (four containers), --max-cost 30 --max-wall-clock 90m, factory at 3b025bbd.

FIRST MILESTONE, +3min: exit 7 is dead. Worker 201's own log — readable at all only because of tick 0fg — shows the full boot succeeding:

  ticks-worker-probe-ok tick=201 tk=dev harness=omp
  model workers-ai/@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731 (from the control plane)   <- ys3's fix
  model route workers-ai -> .../api/gateway/workers-ai/v1 as @cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-flash-0731
  model probe green: answered a one-token request through the gateway (HTTP 200)
  harness probe green: omp answered 'READY' through its 'cloudflare-ai-gateway' provider
  3 of 3 environment checks green
  starting the omp harness on tick 201 (branch tick/72y/201)

'(from the control plane)' is the load-bearing phrase: TICKS_MODEL now comes from workerBootEnv's default rather than the checkout's [roles.implement], which is exactly what ys3 changed. Three worker streams were present at the 3-minute mark (201, 5jo, 5qj at 2357 bytes each), so the fan-out is real and concurrent, not one container at a time.

Repository setup took 0s on a warm cache — worth noting against kuf's finding that dependency install, not image pull, was the whole of the 3.74x fan-out degradation at N=5.
2026-08-22 14:12 - +25min: the workers are doing real work, and the cache numbers are a headline finding.

MODEL LOOP CONFIRMED. tk cloud trace shows 393 model calls with genuine tool use — reading cloud/factory/src/run-workflow.ts and internal/herd/dashboard/model.go, running vitest, grepping for MAX_OBSERVATIONS. deepseek-v4-flash drives the omp loop competently. Every prior claim that a Workers AI model could sustain the loop rested on the orchestrator's deepseek-v4-pro; this is the first evidence for flash as an IMPLEMENTER.

PROMPT CACHE 95-99%, sustained across calls 377-393. Compare y45's recorded reality for the orchestrator tier: v4-pro delivered roughly half its post-warm opportunities and real runs sat at 60-65%, which fxf attributed largely to instance-side routing. flash is hitting 95.6-99.4%. That matches y45's probe (flash 23/23 post-warm hits, v4-pro 12/24) and it means the per-tick cost model built on 60-65% is pessimistic for worker containers by a wide margin. Cached input costs 0.004 neurons against 0.120 uncached, so this is close to a 30x difference on the cached portion.

OBSERVATION TO CHASE (not a blocker): worker log streams froze at 4631 bytes once the harness started — every stream's last line is 'Working...'. So tick 0fg streams the BOOT reliably, which is what it was for and what made the exit-7 diagnosis instant, but the harness's own stdout is not reaching R2 the way the orchestrator sandbox's does. File as a follow-up after this run settles.

Also: tick gm5 has no log stream at all, while 201, 5jo and 5qj all do. Either it never dispatched or it died before the stream opened. Resolve against the persisted wave outcomes (ys3's writeWaveOutcomes) when the run ends.
2026-08-22 14:41 - RUN 1 VERDICT (run_2e66e765f74c4192b2b9a24a6e8415cf): the substrate works; the worker BUDGET does not.

What is now proven, and was never proven before:
- Per-tick worker containers boot green. Zero exit-7 boots. ys3's fix holds against the live factory.
- Fan-out is real and concurrent: 3 containers (201, 5jo, 5qj) booted, cloned, passed pre-flight and ran the omp harness simultaneously.
- Each container's own log is readable per tick (0fg), which is how the boot was verified at all.
- deepseek-v4-flash sustains a real agentic loop: 393+ calls, real tool use, 95-99% prompt cache.
- Each container pushed a branch (tick/72y/201, /5jo, /5qj) and a durable report.

What failed: every worker was killed at exit 124 after ~29 minutes with ZERO work commits. CLOUD_WAVE_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS is 30 minutes and the harness budget derives from it. Filed as 5fg, which now blocks this tick. The failure mode is the worst-value one available — the run paid for 393 model calls of real work and kept none of it — but it is a budget constant, not a substrate defect.

Also unresolved: tick gm5 never opened a log stream and never pushed a branch, while its three wave-mates all did. Determine from the persisted wave outcomes whether it was dispatched at all.

Wave 2 was NOT reached, so wiy's every-wave fan-out is still unproven live: with no wave-1 tick completing, there was no next wave to derive. Re-run after 5fg.
2026-08-22 15:28 - gm5 EXPLAINED — not a defect. cloud/factory/wrangler.toml sets [[containers]] max_instances = 3, and resolveDispatchWidth narrows the wave's CONCURRENCY to that deployment ceiling (recorded as cloud_wave:width=3:capped), while .tick/runners.toml asks for max_parallel = 6. So a 4-tick wave runs three containers at a time and queues the fourth. gm5 was queued behind 201/5jo/5qj, and in run 1 I hard-stopped the run before a slot ever freed. Nothing was silently dropped.

Worth carrying into Phase 3 planning rather than fixing here: the effective fan-out ceiling of this deployment is 3, not the 6 the repository asks for, so kuf's N=5 degradation curve cannot currently be reproduced on this factory.

RUN 1 COST: $0.62 for 393+ model calls across three containers — well inside budget, and a useful datapoint against y45's $4.47 for a complete one-tick epic on v4-pro. The 95-99% cache rate is doing most of that work.

RUN 1 POSTSCRIPT: its workflow ended 'errored' and the run sat in 'stopping' indefinitely, holding nothing — the lease moved to run 2 correctly at 13:22:50, so this did not block anything. A run that can never reach 'stopped' is still a state-machine loose end worth a look in Phase 3.
2026-08-22 17:01 - RUN 2 VERDICT (run_9e40b9563bfb493cac1fe6625356e538): the workers were never the problem. The SUPERVISOR was dead from minute ~10.

Queried the Workflow instance directly instead of inferring from the run record:
  status: errored | error: Execution timed out after 600000ms | last step: cloud:dispatch:0-1

Cloudflare Workflows caps a step's execution at 10 minutes. dispatchWave blocks inside one step.do() until the whole wave settles, so the cloud-wave path kills its own supervisor on any wave longer than ten minutes. Filed as 2xm, which now blocks this tick. Run 1 errored identically — both runs, same message, same step.

What run 2 still proved, and it is not nothing:
- Zero exit-7 boots again, on a second independent run. ys3 holds.
- Three containers concurrent, 1062+ model calls, cache 94-99% sustained on deepseek-v4-flash.
- Worker budget correctly raised: workers ran ~40 minutes of model work against the old 29-minute kill, so 5fg took effect.
- Per-tick logs (0fg) again made the boot verifiable in seconds.

What is still unproven, and honestly cannot be claimed: no branch was ever collected, no wave 2 was derived, so wiy's every-wave fan-out and the ready-to-merge half of this tick's acceptance remain untested. The containers went on working orphaned until 14:02, long after their supervisor died at ~13:32, and nothing collected them.

Cost of both runs together: ~$1.60. Cheap for the finding — this defect had been hiding behind ys3's exit 7 the whole time, and it would have hidden behind the next hypothesis too if I had kept reading the run record instead of the Workflow instance.
2026-08-22 18:01 - RUN 3 (run_215b7cbff9dd405c80d738be45cccde5) started 15:46:47Z — 3 containers (201, 5jo, 5qj), factory at 16a0d262, --max-cost 40 --max-wall-clock 3h.

MILESTONE at +14min, the one both previous runs failed: THE SUPERVISOR IS ALIVE PAST THE 10-MINUTE CAP.

  WORKFLOW STATUS: running
  error: null
  steps: cloud:dispatch:0-1, cloud:dispatch:0:1-1, cloud:dispatch:0:2-1

Runs 1 and 2 were both 'errored / Execution timed out after 600000ms' by this point, with cloud:dispatch:0-1 as their last step. Run 3 shows leg 0 (dispatch) followed by watch legs 1 and 2, exactly the bounded-step shape tick 2xm built. This is the first cloud run whose workers AND supervisor can both survive a real wave.
2026-08-22 19:23 - RUN 3 VERDICT (run_215b7cbff9dd405c80d738be45cccde5, 15:46:47Z -> ~17:20Z, 3 containers, ~$1.4):

THE SUBSTRATE IS PROVEN. Every mechanism Phase 2 built worked, live, for the first time in one run:
- Supervisor survived: workflow reached step 36 and went on into closeout. Runs 1 and 2 were dead by step 5. 2xm holds.
- Zero exit-7 boots, third run running. ys3 holds.
- Three containers concurrent, all three pushed branches with reports. Fan-out is real.
- Per-tick logs readable throughout (0fg).
- 5fg's SALVAGE fired live and worked: 5qj was killed at the bound with 4 uncommitted paths and they are now commit adfedff5 on its branch instead of being destroyed with the container. That is the exact failure run 1 lost 393 model calls to.

PER-CONTAINER OUTCOME:
  201  exit 124 (bound), 0 work commits, nothing to salvage
  5jo  exit 0,   2 work commits — real, correct work (e0898b00 qualifies herdr agent names per repo) plus one illegal 'tk close' commit (filed as dxk)
  5qj  exit 124 (bound), 0 work commits, 4 paths salvaged into adfedff5

THE REMAINING LIMIT IS THE MODEL, NOT THE SUBSTRATE. Two of three ticks did not finish inside 90 minutes on deepseek-v4-flash. These are not toy ticks — 201 is scrolling in a bubbletea TUI, 5qj is a workerd lifecycle problem in vitest — and flash ground through 90 minutes of 94-99%-cached calls without converging. y45 already predicted this shape: it put flash at implement.balanced/economy and deepseek-v4-pro at implement.strong.

So this tick's acceptance bar ('>=3 ready-to-merge') is NOT met, and I am not going to claim it is. Next run routes workers at deepseek-v4-pro — still Workers AI, still credit-funded, and y45's own recommendation for the strong implement tier — with a longer budget. If pro converges where flash did not, that is also the measurement y45 left owed.

Also filed from this run: dxk (a worker wrote tracker state despite the prompt forbidding it) and 3gr (a worker that exits 0 with work commits but no report is told to re-dispatch).
2026-08-22 23:46 - RUN 4 (run_b42d0eb618114ddb8787ed93ed1192ef, 18:04:03Z -> 19:38:39Z, 3 containers on deepseek-v4-pro, $9.64): THE FULL LOOP CLOSED.

  workflow: complete        <- not 'errored', not 'running forever'
  run state: stopped, ended_at set

Per container:
  201  exit 0, 1 work commit (2a1fc51b 'herd dashboard: scroll board to follow cursor'), STATUS: PASS
  4qx  exit 0, 1 work commit (126a58b0 'herd/collect: fix phantom boundary violation'), STATUS: DONE
  5qj  no branch pushed

201 is the direct A/B: deepseek-v4-flash failed it twice at the 90-minute bound in runs 1 and 3; v4-pro finished it. 1cd's model change is measured, not asserted.

AND THE ORCHESTRATOR MERGED THEM ITSELF. origin/tick-run/72y carries both workers' commits plus its own merge (828ad8e6). Dispatch -> container -> real work -> push -> collect -> merge -> run branch, with no local orchestrator involved. That is the Phase 2 deliverable working end to end.

Both agents also wrote their OWN reports with real status lines — no fallback needed — and dxk's guard is confirmed live in every worker's boot log: 'boundary guard installed: the agent's tk refuses, and a commit staging .tick/ is rejected'. No tracker-state commit appeared on any branch this run.

Against this tick's acceptance: 3 containers in wave 1 (met), zero exit-7 boots (met), per-container outcome and cost recorded (met), >=3 ready-to-merge (NOT met — 2). 5qj did not push. One more run to settle the third.
acceptance_criteria: One cloud run, >=3 worker containers in wave 1, >=3 branches ready-to-merge, zero exit-7 boots, and a note on this tick recording per-container outcome, wall-clock and cost.
